title: [R3-4] Reach the Foundation provider with its sealed context from a production-launched daemon
description:
FILED FROM THE THIRD HUMAN REVIEW OF PR #3 (anchored d01c3316, 2026-08-28: 'Request changes - do not merge', 12 P1 merge blockers + P2 follow-ups). Re-verified at HEAD a09b11fa by a read-only verifier; see the ruling memo in the epic channel. Reviewer's finding: R3-4 foundation dispatch unreachable. Existing rows checked: task-203a5ca7aada4375a98a95df8773e249(BLOCKED) closesIt=true, task-e7c1875f22dc455a918b0ceb7f82f69a(REVIEW) closesIt=true, task-fcdc272dbf5040c7803c73340ed69229(BLOCKED) closesIt=false, task-40a53880e25f4a72911df6f33b39960a(DONE) closesIt=false, task-fc9660b0a4f24891908a11e303a7c347(PLANNING) closesIt=false, task-c289b8fbcb9840968a9b3994e73b79a4(BLOCKED) closesIt=false. Gap this row closes: No row makes the seal REACHABLE in a production-launched daemon. task-203a5ca7 wires the seal from a host-scoped env key (MOE_PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_DIGEST) and declares 'absent = valid, fall back to the refusing port'; nothing composes that key: moe-up-env.ts:93-102 builds the daemon overlay without it (and without the two sibling catalog keys), and windows-project-stack-boundary.ts:33-49 PROJECT_STACK_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS is a closed allowlist that would strip it. So after 203a5ca7 + e7c1875f land, `moe up` / project-stack daemons still refuse every real dispatch with FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_SEAL_UNCONFIGURED - the reviewer's first sentence persists in deployment. Secondary gaps: (a) the remediation epic epic-072d85be has no row adopting/verifying R3-4 (P1); the owning rows live in epic-e0c54bdd and epic-bd387eeb and 203a5ca7 is BLOCKED on a stale reason (its named prerequisite a283eb8f is at HEAD) with its step-2/3 bytes uncommitted in the shared worktree, exposed to a session-end sweep; (b) no row proves end to end, from a daemon composed by createStoreDependencies(readStoreDependencyEnv(process.env)), that the bytes at the runner boundary equal the durable contextManifestDigest - 203a5ca7 step 6 injects the digest in-test at the registry, not through the process env path.

REVIEWER (PR #3 review 3 at d01c3316, P1 R3-4): Foundation dispatch is unreachable; even if wired, the provider does not receive its sealed context. Production constructs command ports without foundationContextSeal, so the fallback refuses every real dispatch with FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_SEAL_UNCONFIGURED (daemon-store-dependencies.ts:133-174; daemon-command-async-entries.ts:42-53). With a seal injected, the service still launches from caller-supplied request.launchTemplate, ignoring context.template and context.bytes (foundation-attempt-service.ts:343-369). The produced argv contains only flags, while the runner passes only executable/argv/cwd/environment and drops provider stdin (launch-template-producer.ts:104-110; claude-launcher.ts:325-334). Later evidence can cite a context digest for bytes the provider never saw.

RE-MEASURED AT HEAD a09b11fa (stale by default, re-measure at claim): none of the five cited files changed since d01c3316; all four mechanisms hold at the cited lines. daemon-store-dependencies.ts:162-169 passes no foundationContextSeal; daemon-command-async-entries.ts:49 falls back to unconfiguredFoundationContextSealPort(); foundation-attempt-service.ts:343-352 seals then :365-368 launches `{ ...request.launchTemplate, cwd }` never reading context.template/bytes/contextManifestDigest; composeArgv is flags-only. Post-review commit a283eb8f (task-e7c1875f, REVIEW) made the runner write request.renderedContext to providerStdin (claude-launcher-lifecycle.ts:77-97) and widened REQUEST_KEYS to 17 (claude-launcher-input.ts:16-18), but foundation-attempt-contracts.ts:206-218 launchRequestBody still emits 15 keys, so on win32 every daemon-composed launch now refuses CLAUDE_LAUNCH_REQUEST_MALFORMED before any boundary opens (20 disclosed daemon reds). ENV GAP: task-203a5ca7 steps 2-3 (uncommitted WIP in the shared worktree: dirty daemon-store-dependencies.ts + untracked daemon-context-seal-wiring.{ts,js,test.ts}) wire the seal from MOE_PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_DIGEST and treat an absent key as valid-unconfigured; `git grep MOE_PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_DIGEST HEAD` = 0; moe-up-env.ts:93-102 composes the daemon overlay from only MOE_STORE_PATH/MOE_PROJECT_ID/MOE_DAEMON_CREDENTIAL/MOE_AGENT_COMMAND/provider credentials; windows-project-stack-boundary.ts:33-49 PROJECT_STACK_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS is a closed allowlist that omits it (and MOE_VERIFICATION_CATALOG, MOE_FOUNDATION_WORKSPACE_CATALOG). So once 203a5ca7 and e7c1875f land, a `moe up` or project-stack daemon STILL refuses every real dispatch on the fallback port.

OWNED ELSEWHERE - ADOPT, NEVER DUPLICATE: seal-port wiring + launchRequestBody/call-site rewrite + registry-level accepted control = task-203a5ca7 (BLOCKED on a STALE reason: its prerequisite runner change a283eb8f is at HEAD; ask the governor to lift, do not re-implement); runner stdin delivery = task-e7c1875f (REVIEW); admission split = task-fcdc272d (sequenced after 203a5ca7). THIS ROW owns only what no row covers: composing the configuration digest into the production daemon process env (moe-up overlay + project-stack allowlist, or a justified store-derived fallback at boot), and a real-process end-to-end control proving bytes at the runner boundary equal the durable digest from a daemon composed by createStoreDependencies(readStoreDependencyEnv(process.env)).
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK at claim, on disk, before any edit: task-e7c1875f is DONE with a283eb8f an ancestor of HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor a283eb8f HEAD`), task-203a5ca7 is DONE, `git grep -n "context.template" HEAD -- apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-contracts.ts apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-service.ts` is non-empty, `git grep -n foundationContextSeal HEAD -- apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.ts apps/daemon/src/daemon-context-seal-wiring.ts` is non-empty, and the key count emitted by launchRequestBody equals REQUEST_KEYS.length (17). If any premise fails, moe.report_blocked naming the row and the failing probe; never re-implement 203a5ca7 steps 2-5 or commit its uncommitted WIP under this id. Record every probe's exact output in a task comment.

The production daemon env composer (apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/moe-up-env.ts overlay) and the Windows project-stack allowlist (packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-project-stack-boundary.ts PROJECT_STACK_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS) both carry MOE_PROJECT_CONFIGURATION_DIGEST (and, if the seal's catalog inputs are likewise absent, MOE_VERIFICATION_CATALOG / MOE_FOUNDATION_WORKSPACE_CATALOG), sourced from the durable current project configuration's settingsDigest - never typed by hand and never defaulted; a missing durable configuration surfaces as a stable refusal code at launch, not a silent fall-through to the unconfigured port. DRILL (moe-up-env.test.ts arm named for the key): delete the overlay entry -> the arm asserting the composed overlay names the key with a 64-hex value reds; force a non-hex value -> the daemon-context-seal-wiring HEX64 refusal arm reds; remove the allowlist entry alone -> the project-stack boundary env-filter arm reds while the moe-up overlay arm stays green (

A real-process control (extend the foundation e2e harness under task-05f12b4f's authority, run from PowerShell): boot the daemon through the production entry (createStoreDependencies(readStoreDependencyEnv(process.env))) with the composed env, submit one authenticated foundation.dispatch, and assert (i) the outcome is neither FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_SEAL_UNCONFIGURED nor CLAUDE_LAUNCH_REQUEST_MALFORMED, (ii) the bytes captured at the runner boundary's providerStdin are byte-equal to readSealedFoundationContext(...).bytes read back from the store, and (iii) the contextManifestDigest on the launch evidence equals the durable record's digest. DRILL: revert the service call site to request.launchTemplate using a caller template whose argv and renderedContext DIFFER from the sealed one -> the byte-equality arm reds (if caller and sealed are identical the drill is vacuous - vary them, or report the finding); drop the env key -> the arm reds with FOUNDATION_CONTEXT_SEAL_UNCONFIGURED and the record

Fail-closed negatives preserved unchanged: with the digest key absent the daemon still boots and serves every non-Foundation command kind (203a5ca7's 'absent is valid' state), and unconfiguredFoundationContextSealPort's code and layer are untouched; daemon-command-async-entries.ts:49's fallback is not removed. DRILL: delete the fallback `?? unconfiguredFoundationContextSealPort()` -> the existing unconfigured-refusal arm reds (proves the fence is still load-bearing), restore proven by empty `git diff -- apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-async-entries.ts`.

Gates, each standalone and unpiped with exit code and nonzero Test Files/Tests lines recorded in a task comment: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` (quote the `$ tsc` echo), `pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck`, the focused daemon suites (activation-telemetry-launch.test.ts, activation-run-commit.test.ts, work/launch-template-producer.test.ts, work/foundation-attempt-windows.test.ts, work/foundation-context-launch-control.test.ts, the new e2e lane) all GREEN at the delivered commit - the 20 reds disclosed on task-e7c1875f must be gone, attributed by path if any foreign red remains; explicit-pathspec commit of owned paths only; completion comment names R3-4, task-203a5ca7, task-e7c1875f, task-fcdc272d and records every drill's red arm title and restore proof.
taskRails: Adopt, never duplicate: the seal wiring, launchRequestBody rewrite, call-site replacement and registry-level accepted control belong to task-203a5ca7; runner stdin delivery to task-e7c1875f; admission split to task-fcdc272d. If 203a5ca7 is still BLOCKED on the stale 'runner does not admit the keys' reason, route a lift request to the governor rather than re-doing its steps.

Never commit the peer's uncommitted 203a5ca7 WIP (dirty apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.ts; untracked apps/daemon/src/daemon-context-seal-wiring.ts/.js/.test.ts) under this row's id; explicit pathspec only, and `git status --porcelain` the exact paths before every commit.
Never loosen REQUEST_KEYS / snapshotExactRecord to admit a 15-key body, and @moe/runner gains no @moe/context dependency - the digest is carried verbatim, never recomputed runner-side.

Absent-env stays fail-closed: no default digest, no 'skip the seal' branch, no provider launch without a durable context record committed first (foundation-attempt-service.ts ordering comment at :330-343 is a safety property).

Line caps: daemon-store-dependencies.ts is at/over the 400 split bound (408 per 203a5ca7's plan) and foundation-attempt-service.ts is at 397 - add nothing to either; new logic goes in a sibling module with an exact-LF `.js` bridge.
P1 merge blocker under epic-072d85be rails; measure first, claim last (the reaper releases long PLANNING claims); drills vary ONE degree of freedom with the red arm's title naming the mechanism.
Adopt, never duplicate: re-measure the cited lines at claim time; if a sibling row landed the mechanism first, verify and close rather than re-implement.
